findings.reason: unnamed, the worker must invent a dispatch-time source, and an invented one is a second definition of "when this review was dispatched" that no other reader shares.
findings.text: condition 4 ("its modification time is after this review's dispatch") names no source for the dispatch instant, while `run_id_dispatch_time` (reckon/crew/review.py:2584) and `run_record_times` (reckon/crew/review.py:2541) already derive a run's dispatch time from its id and its record

findings.reason: a second head comparison drifts from the owner it copies (the owner deliberately accepts legacy records whose head is reconstructed, which the new strict-equality predicate would refuse), so the watcher and promotion can disagree about one record.
findings.text: the section adds a head predicate ("its reviewed_head_sha equals that head") inside the delivery reader, duplicating the shared head-keyed selection `select_review_for_head` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:111) with `review_described_head` (:80) and `same_revision` (:102) that promotion and the classifier already share; §2 duplicates the same derivation a second time by re-implementing the head-from-path reading in a new script rather than importing `_review_record_subject` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:133)

findings.reason: the section must account for the public definitions the script's module-level functions add before the node is built.
findings.text: the section adds a new script (`scripts/review_rows_with_another_rounds_verdict.py`) and a new doc without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be, against this week's counts

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design puts the whole decision behind the single existing function `_delivered_review_record` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py:236) so every reader inherits one predicate, which is depth rather than surface; the only caveat is the §1 claim that "no reader gains a check of its own" is slightly overstated, since the "no head-keyed path is reported, not promoted" refusal lands in the watcher/acceptance path (reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:314).
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the section re-derives a head-keyed selection and a head-from-path derivation that shared owners already provide.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1814, cli_options 364, mcp_views 34, refusal_families 23; §2 adds a new script and doc without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites `_review_subject` and the declared write paths, but the predicate it proposes needs a dispatch instant and a head comparison whose existing owners (`run_id_dispatch_time`, `select_review_for_head`) it does not cite.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §1 extends existing machinery in place rather than wrapping it; there is no new forwarding layer, and §3 adds nothing yet.
